kp9:1.2: What should be done by one skilful in good, who has comprehended the state of peace:
kp9:1.4: he ought to be able, straight, and upright, easy to speak to, meek, without conceit,
kp9:2.2: satisfied (with little), easy to support, free from duties, and light in living,
kp9:2.4: with faculties at peace, prudent, not forward, and greedless among the families,
kp9:3.2: he should not do the slightest thing whereby others who are wise might find fault (with him).
kp9:3.4: “(May all beings) be happy and secure, may all beings in their hearts be happy!
kp9:4.2: Whatsoever breathing beings there are - trembling, firm, or any other (beings),
kp9:4.4: whether they be long or great, of middle size, short, tiny, or of compact (body),
kp9:5.2: those who are seen, and those who are unseen, those who live far away, those who are near,
kp9:5.4: those who are born, and those who still seek birth - may all beings in their hearts be happy!”
kp9:6.2: No one should cheat another, nor should he despise anyone wherever they be,
kp9:6.4: he should not long for suffering for another because of anger or resentment.
kp9:7.2: In the same way as a mother would protect her son, her only son, with her life,
kp9:7.4: so toward all beings he should develop the measureless thought (of friendliness).
kp9:8.2: Towards the whole wide world he should develop the measureless thought of friendliness,
kp9:8.3: above, below, and across (the middle), without barriers, hate, or enemy.
kp9:9.1: Standing, walking, sitting, lying, for as long as he is without torpor,
kp9:9.4: he should be resolved on this mindfulness, for this, they say here, is the (true) spiritual life.
kp9:10.2: Without going back to (wrong) views, virtuous, and endowed with (true) insight,
kp9:10.4: having removed (all) greed for sense pleasures, he will never come to lie in a womb again.
